claims.text: As-sintered TiB2 components have inherent surface porosity.
As-sintered TiB2 components contain grain-boundary networks that act as diffusion paths for molten aluminum.
Pack siliconizing TiB2 at approximately 900°C for 2 hours can produce a silicon-enriched surface layer.
Silicon diffuses into the near-surface region of TiB2 during the proposed siliconizing treatment.
The proposed treatment can create a continuous and adherent silicon-rich modified surface layer.
Contact between the silicon-rich layer and molten aluminum promotes formation of a thin, stable intermetallic or silicate barrier.
The silicon-enriched layer reacts with molten aluminum to form a stable Al-Si-rich compound.
The resulting Al-Si-rich compound acts as a diffusion barrier.
The proposed barrier reduces aluminum infiltration along pre-existing microstructural defects in TiB2.
The proposed barrier reduces corrosion of TiB2 during molten-aluminum exposure.
Siliconized TiB2 components will have significantly lower weight loss than untreated as-sintered TiB2 during otherwise identical molten-aluminum exposure.
Siliconized TiB2 components will have shallower corrosion penetration than untreated as-sintered TiB2.
Untreated as-sintered TiB2 has higher molten-aluminum corrosion susceptibility because of its porosity and continuous grain-boundary networks.
The intervention should remain effective in molten aluminum at approximately 660°C under standard hot-dip aluminum-plating exposure conditions.
The intervention may become less effective if the siliconized layer is discontinuous.
The intervention may become less effective if service conditions exceed the stability range of the protective barrier.
The proposed mechanism is supported by analogous high-temperature siliconizing treatments.
